akhfash:1-1.t: He said ﴿قۤ وَٱلْقُرْآنِ ٱلْمَجِيدِ﴾: an oath upon ﴿قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ ٱلأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ﴾ [4].

akhfash:3-3.t: And He said ﴿أَإِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَاباً ذَلِكَ رَجْعُ بَعِيدٌ﴾: He did not mention "that it is a return"; that is — and Allah knows best — because it was in answer, as though it had been said to them: "You will return". So they said: "When we have become dust? That is a far return."

akhfash:15-15.t: And He said ﴿بَلْ هُمْ فِي لَبْسٍ﴾ because you say: "لَبَسْتُ عليه لَبْساً" (I confused it for him).

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ﴾: He means "more in control of him and nearer to him in power over him".

akhfash:17-17.t: And He said ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ قَعِيدٌ﴾ and did not say "on the right a seated one and on the left a seated one"; He mentioned one of them and it sufficed, as He said ﴿يُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلاً﴾, where the singular sufficed for the plural, and as He said ﴿فَإِن طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَن شَيْءٍ مِّنْهُ نَفْساً﴾.
